p.title: From dynastic empire to nation-state
p.challenge: Arrange the 5 steps that show how France became a nation of citizens

nodes.info: Earlier, much of Europe was ruled by dynastic empires: one ruling family held many different peoples together.
Sovereignty (supreme power) passes from the monarch to the body of French citizens.
Ideas of la patrie and le citoyen, the tricolour, a National Assembly, uniform laws, weights and measures, no internal customs duties, Parisian French as the common language.
The Civil Code ended privileges based on birth, made all equal before the law and secured the right to property.
Higher taxes, censorship and forced conscription made many people in conquered lands hostile to French rule.

Choose Yes or No.
Choose Yes or No.

nodes.text: No vote: women were left out
nodes.info: Women could not vote or be elected.
Men without property were left out too.
Only property-owning men got the right to vote and to be elected.

p.title: Gandhiji's plan for Non-Cooperation
p.challenge: Follow the movement stage by stage. At the question, decide what comes next

nodes.text: Hind Swaraj: British rule needs our cooperation
nodes.info: In Hind Swaraj (1909) Gandhiji argued British rule survived only because Indians cooperated.
Calcutta session (Sept 1920) agreed to non-cooperation for Khilafat and swaraj; Nagpur adopted it. The movement began in January 1921.
The first step was to surrender titles given by the government.
Boycott of civil services, army, police, courts, councils, schools and foreign goods. Imports of foreign cloth fell from ₹102 crore to ₹57 crore (1921 to 1922).
Choose what happens.
That was the plan. In reality Gandhiji withdrew the movement in February 1922 after violence at Chauri Chaura.

The UN Monetary and Financial Conference at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA.

nodes.text: IMF and World Bank set up
nodes.info: IMF: deals with members' external surpluses and deficits. World Bank: finances post-war reconstruction.
The US emerges as the dominant economic, political and military power.
Fixed exchange rates; the US dollar anchored to gold at $35 per ounce.
They demand a New International Economic Order (NIEO): control over resources, fairer prices, better market access.

nodes.info: The merchant clothier bought wool from a wool stapler.
The merchant took the wool to spinners in the countryside.
Merchants, not the workers, controlled the whole chain.
This was proto-industrialisation: large-scale production for an international market, not in factories.

events.info: From about AD 594, paper was rubbed on inked woodblocks; folded into 'accordion books'.

events.label: Hand printing reaches Japan
events.info: Brought by Buddhist missionaries from China around AD 768-770.

events.label: Diamond Sutra printed in Japan
events.info: The oldest Japanese book: six sheets of text with woodcut illustrations.

events.label: Marco Polo returns to Italy

events.label: Gutenberg perfects his press
events.info: His first book, the Bible: about 180 copies in three years.

events.label: Presses in most of Europe
events.info: Between 1450 and 1550 presses spread across Europe, making books cheaper.
